text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on March 16 in history:
37 - Roman Emperor Tiberius, having retired to Capri, died on a visit to the mainland near the Bay of Naples.
1751 - James Madison, American statesman and fourth U.S. president (1809-1817), born. He was the first and only president to exercise his rank as commander-in-chief in an actual battle.
1787 - Georg Ohm, German physicist, born. He gave his name to the unit which measures electrical resistance.

1792 - Gustavus III of Sweden was shot by Captain Anckarstroem at a masked ball. He died on March 29. His rule was known as the "Gustavian Enlightenment" and he was a great patron of the arts. Giuseppe Verdi composed his opera "A Masked Ball" around these events.
1802 - The United States Congress passed an act establishing a military academy at West Point, New York.
1827 - Freedom's Journal, the first newspaper for blacks in the United States, was published in New York.
1851 - Spain signed a concordat with the Papacy under which Roman Catholicism became the only authorised faith. It also gave control of education and the press to the Church.

1878 - William Banting, English undertaker and slimming pioneer, died. Forced to diet, he listed his methods in his "Letter on Corpulence" (1863). The letter's popularity led to the word "banting", meaning to diet.
1898 - Aubrey Vincent Beardsley, British artist and illustrator, died of consumption. Together with Oscar Wilde, he was prominent in the "Aesthetic" movement" of the end of the century. He was 25.

1917 - In Russia, Grand Duke Michael, brother of former Tsar Nicholas II who had abdicated the day before, refused to take the throne. The provisional government under Prince Georgi Lvov then formally took office.
1926 - First liquid-fuel rocket was successfully launched by Professor Robert Goddard at Auburn, Massachusetts. The rocket travelled 184 feet in 2.5 seconds.
1935 - German leader Adolf Hitler renounced the disarmament clauses in the Versailles Treaty and introduced conscription.

1937 - Sir Joseph Austen Chamberlain, British statesman, died. As British foreign secretary he negotiated the Locarno Pact (1925) and together with U.S. Vice-President Charles Gates Dawes, he won the 1925 Nobel peace prize.
1940 - Bernardo Bertolucci, Italian film director, born. His films included "Last Tango in Paris", "1900" and "The Last Emperor".
1968 - In the Vietnam War, during an operation in the village of My Lai, a platoon of U.S. troops massacred at least 100 Vietnamese civilians.

1973 - In Paris, finance ministers of 14 countries, and the heads of the IMF, OECD and BIS agreed to establish a currency system with backing from the United States, based on floating rates of exchange.
1976 - British Prime Minister Harold Wilson announced his intention to retire. He was succeeded by James Callaghan on April 5.
1978 - Former Italian premier Aldo Moro was kidnapped by Red Brigades guerrillas, who demanded the release of all Communist prisoners.
1978 - About 220,000 tons of oil were spilled after the Amoco Cadiz ran aground off the Britanny coast.
1982 - Soviet President Leonid Brezhnev announced that the Soviet Union was freezing deployment of SS-20 missiles west of the Urals.
1984 - South Africa and Mozambique signed a non-aggression pact near the border town of Komatipoort.
1985 - U.S. journalist Terry Anderson kidnapped in Beirut. He was not released until December 4, 1991 after 2,454 days in captivity.
1995 - Norman Thagard stepped aboard the Mir space station to become the first U.S. astronaut to fly on a Russian spacecraft.
